title: Ekström wins as the title rivals collide at the start
dek: Mattias Ekström won Race 2 at the Hungaroring from Adrien Tambay after Mortara and Wittmann collided at the start, and Wittmann's later exclusion left his title lead unchanged at 14 points.

chapters.title: Audi sweeps Saturday, Wittmann holds on
text: Saturday had belonged to Audi. Edoardo Mortara won Race 1 from pole, Jamie Green and Miguel Molina completed the podium, and the first six places all went to Audi RS 5 DTMs, with Marco Wittmann seventh as the best of the rest. The result cut Wittmann's lead from 33 points to 14, 176 to 162, with Green third on 137 and Robert Wickens fourth on 121. A new qualifying session and a 60-minute race on Sunday gave the title contenders another chance, with three races left, counting that one.

chapters.title: Mortara takes pole again, Wittmann splits the Audis
text: Mortara left his best lap to the last attempt for the second time in the weekend and took pole with a 1m34.984s, a full 0.298 seconds quicker than his Saturday time. He was 0.154 seconds clear of his Abt team-mate Mattias Ekström, who in turn beat Wittmann's BMW for second place by a single thousandth of a second, 1m35.138s to 1m35.139s.

Audi did not have everything its own way this time. Wittmann's Team RMG BMW was the third-fastest car, ahead of Green, who was 0.161 seconds off pole, and Molina. Maxime Martin and Tom Blomqvist put the RBM BMWs sixth and seventh, and Wickens was eighth, four-tenths behind Mortara. He was the only Mercedes in the top ten, with Daniel Juncadella 11th. Adrien Tambay qualified 10th for Audi and António Félix da Costa 12th.
Further back it was another hard session for Mercedes. Paul di Resta was 21st, Gary Paffett 22nd, Maximilian Götz 23rd and Felix Rosenqvist last of the 24 cars, 1.078 seconds slower than Mortara.

chapters.title: A false start, then Mortara and Wittmann collide
text: The race began twice. Wickens, who had qualified eighth, went to the wrong side of the grid at the end of the formation lap, forcing the start to be aborted and a second formation lap to be run.

When the lights went out Mortara spun his wheels and Wittmann, directly behind him on the grid, moved alongside on the outside. Mortara moved across and Wittmann was pushed onto the grass, got ahead after rejoining, and then made contact with the Audi again. The BMW was sent sideways into the side of Green, who was alongside Mortara. Wittmann straightened up and continued, while Mortara had a puncture and pitted at the end of the lap. Green pulled into the pits and did not continue. Both title rivals received warnings for the incident.
Ekström, who had made a clean start from second, took the lead ahead of Tambay, who made up eight places from 10th, while Juncadella jumped from 11th to third.

chapters.title: Ekström controls the stops, Wittmann repasses Félix da Costa
text: The first lap had left large gaps, so little changed when the pit stops came. Tambay stopped first, two laps before Ekström, who came in on lap 24 and rejoined in the lead. Tambay had closed up a little during the stops but could not threaten the Swede for long.

Wittmann, running with a damaged car and a string of BMWs behind him, dropped behind Félix da Costa during the stops, then passed his fellow BMW driver on the track to regain the place. Further back Scheider passed Martin late in the race. Mortara, meanwhile, ran at the back of the field after his stop and was never in contention for points.

chapters.title: Ekström wins from Tambay on the road
text: Ekström completed the 36 laps 4.350 seconds ahead of Tambay, with the pair well clear of the rest. Félix da Costa was classified third for BMW, 24.209 seconds behind the winner, ahead of Blomqvist, Glock, Scheider, Martin, Rockenfeller, Tomczyk and Wickens, who took the last point in tenth. The fastest lap of the race went to Ekström, a 1m36.538s on lap 26.

Mortara was classified 19th, three laps down, and Green, Müller and Farfus were all out within the first eight laps. Wittmann and Juncadella both completed the 36 laps but were not classified, because of what the technical delegate found after the flag.

chapters.title: Wittmann and Juncadella excluded, the title race reopens
text: A few hours after the race the stewards removed Wittmann and Juncadella from the results. The technical delegate found that the skid pads on both cars were too low under article 3.22.4 of the technical regulations. That promoted Félix da Costa to third and moved every driver behind the two excluded cars up, which gave Wickens tenth and a single point. BMW and Mercedes first announced appeals, but both withdrew them within days. BMW's motorsport director Jens Marquardt said the team wanted the sport to decide the title, adding they did not want it "decided in court", while Mercedes said it did not expect an appeal to succeed.

The exclusion left Wittmann on 176 points, because he scored nothing on Sunday, and his lead over Mortara at 14 points, with Mortara on 162. Green stayed in contention 39 points behind on 137, while Wickens, 54 behind on 122, could no longer catch Wittmann with at most 50 points available at Hockenheim. Ekström was fifth in the standings on 107 and Blomqvist sixth on 105.

Audi's mood was mixed. Its DTM head Dieter Gass said the start was unfortunate and that Mortara's wheelspin had set off the chain, adding that "you can't really blame anyone either". Ekström, who took the 22nd win of his DTM career and his first of 2016, said his race had been quiet, and that he had hoped to end his season well, because he was going to miss the finale to concentrate on the World Rallycross Championship. Wickens admitted that his grid mistake had ended his own title chances, and Mercedes said the incident had effectively ruled it out of the drivers' fight.

That left three men in the championship, Wittmann, Mortara and Green, going into the Hockenheim finale on 15 and 16 October. With 2016 being a season of 18 races over nine weekends, only two races remained, and Wittmann needed to defend a 14-point lead over Mortara.

facts.v: Ekström won from second on the grid, his first victory of 2016 and the 22nd of his DTM career, and he missed the Hockenheim finale to race in World Rallycross.
